Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Primary goal: integrate models into customer-facing scoring flows with <=150ms P95 inference where possible, batch path for async enrichment.
- Quality bar: human-evaluated helpfulness and safety across our canonical prompt set; any regression >2-3% on our rubric is a blocker.
- Constraints: sensitive PII, prefer private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated; procurement timeline: 6–8 weeks.

Proposed next steps (agreed on call)
1) Redwood runs a focused model-fit eval using your prompt set (attached fintechco_prompt_set_v1.txt). We'll benchmark a shortlist of models (Llama-2-13B-Chat, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B-Instruct, and one tuned 13B variant) across accuracy/helpfulness and latency/throughput.
2) Quantization/throughput trade study: we will compare AWQ (4-bit), GPTQ (4-bit post-training), and FP8 (8-bit float where available) on quality delta + throughput uplift.
3) Deliverable: a one-page recommendation, benchmark CSV, and the quant trade-study PDF by EOD Friday (Mar 6).
4) Follow-up call: propose Mon Mar 9 to review results and iterate on any failure modes.

Anything I missed? If this looks good I'll kick off the evals with Aditya and loop Rishi in for any procurement/contract questions.

Thanks Marissa — kicking this off now. Quick note on the shortlist and what we'll measure: 

Model shortlist (initial)
- Llama-2-13B-Chat (base instruct) — good middle ground for instruction-following.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B — strong for instruction tasks, excellent cost profile.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct — high quality on many instruction benchmarks, heavier but useful as a high-water mark.
- Redwood-tuned-13B-v1 (internal tuned variant) — if you want a tuned baseline.

Metrics we'll capture
- Quality: pairwise human eval (helpfulness), automated metrics where sensible (ROUGE/bleu for exact-match prompts), and your rubric pass rate.
- Latency: P50/P95 with typical request sizes from your prompt set.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under continuous batching and Dedicated-like instance.
- Regressions: delta vs a baseline (we'll use Falcon-40B as high-quality baseline for relative regressions).

Quantization trade study plan
- AWQ (4-bit): very promising for throughput on modern kernels; often preserves instruction-following quality but can show small regressions on edge cases.
- GPTQ (4-bit PTQ): fast and widely available toolchain; quality varies by model and needs per-layer calibration — sometimes larger regressions on instruction-based prompts.
- FP8: less aggressive quantization, tends to retain most of the quality while giving a decent throughput uplift when hardware supports FP8 kernels (best on newer GPUs).

Deliverables attached: benchmark-latency-throughput.csv (preview) and quant-trade-study-summary.pdf (summary of expected tradeoffs + initial hypotheses). I'll run the full eval overnight and post final CSV + artifacts tomorrow.

cc: Rishi for procurement context.

Great questions — diving into specifics below. I'll also attach a short table from our preliminary run (see benchmark CSV) and a link to the detailed run artifacts: https://redwood-internal.s3/rdw-2394/quant-study-20260306 (view-only).

1) Quantified regression expectations
- AWQ (4-bit): in our internal runs on instruction-heavy prompts, we typically see <=1.5% absolute drop on human-helpfulness scores vs FP16 baseline for Llama-family models; failure modes tend to be subtle omissions or reduced specificity on long multi-step instructions. For critical prompts (like fraud explanation snippets) we flag anything >1% absolute drop for manual review.
- GPTQ (4-bit PTQ): more variable — ranges from ~0.5% to 4% absolute drop depending on model and the calibration data used; some models show degradation on instruction-following where rewrites or re-prompting helps but isn't ideal.
- FP8: usually within 0.1–0.5% absolute of FP16 quality while delivering ~1.5–2x throughput uplift on supported GPUs.

2) Hardware requirements for FP8
- FP8 kernels are currently supported on NVIDIA Hopper-architecture GPUs and newer (H100 and successors) via optimized runtimes. If you're planning on older Ampere hardware (A100), FP8 support may be limited or require fallback code paths with lower uplift.

3) Hallucination / citation checks
- We'll add a citation-check metric: for prompts that request sources we'll measure hallucination rate (claimed sources that are fabricated) via a combination of automated checks (URL matching) and spot human review.

Next steps from our side for Friday deliverable
- Final CSV with per-model per-quantization metric rows (quality, P50/P95, tokens/sec, hallucination rate).
- Recommendation: if your latency SLO is strict for the sync path, we recommend FP8 on H100-class Dedicated in production for the best quality/throughput balance. For running on less capable hardware or strict cost targets, AWQ provides a strong balance but requires spot-checking of edge-case prompts.

I'll highlight any rows where quality delta >1% for your prompt set so we can review before any rollout.

Thanks — will post the full artifact shortly.
